title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
paragraphs: Rathbone/Bruce-era Sherlock Holmes archive subset spanning selected surviving broadcasts from 1939 through May 1946. The series moved from NBC/Blue to Mutual, changed title in October 1943, and mixed direct Doyle adaptations with new radio stories built from Doyle characters/incidents.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC/Blue Bromo Quinine era (October 2, 1939 to March 1, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Mutual pre-rename era (May 7, 1943 to October 15, 1943) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and The New Adventures era (October 25, 1943 to May 27, 1946) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Arthur Conan Doyle (author, creator, and writer), Basil Rathbone (performer), Nigel Bruce (performer), Anthony Boucher (writer, radio adaptor, and announcer), Denis Green (writer, performer, and radio adaptor), Edna Best (producer), and Harry Bartell (announcer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to deduction and criminal investigation, murder and homicide, espionage, spies and state secrets, disguise and concealed identity, Professor Moriarty and organized criminal plots, and apparent supernatural mystery.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Sherlock Holmes as a long-running radio franchise, Wartime Holmes broadcasts, Sponsor-driven network continuity, and Doyle adaptation and radio expansion.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-halls-of-ivy|The Halls of Ivy]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|crime-classics|Crime Classics]], and [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]].
